description: Fixed corpus and question set for evaluating retrieval and answers. A retrieved chunk counts as relevant when it comes from the expected paper and contains at least one evidence phrase (case-insensitive).

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey

questions.question: What are the two RAG model formulations proposed in the original RAG paper, and how do they differ?
questions.reference: RAG-Sequence uses the same retrieved document to generate the whole output sequence, while RAG-Token can use a different document for each generated token.

questions.question: Which pre-trained model is used as the generator in the original RAG models?
What serves as the non-parametric memory in the original RAG paper?
questions.reference: A dense vector index of Wikipedia, accessed with a pre-trained neural retriever (DPR).

questions.question: How is Wikipedia split into passages for dense passage retrieval?
questions.reference: Articles are split into disjoint text blocks of 100 words, which serve as the basic retrieval units.

questions.question: What kind of negative examples does DPR use during training?
questions.reference: In-batch negatives (the positive passages of other questions in the same batch), combined with hard negatives retrieved by BM25.

questions.question: What architecture does DPR use to encode questions and passages?
questions.reference: Two independent BERT encoders (a dual-encoder), with relevance computed as the dot product of the question and passage embeddings.

questions.question: Where in a long input context do language models use relevant information best?
questions.reference: At the beginning or the end of the context; performance degrades significantly when the relevant information is in the middle.

questions.question: Which tasks were used to study how language models use long contexts?
questions.reference: Multi-document question answering and synthetic key-value retrieval.

questions.question: What special tokens does Self-RAG generate to critique its own outputs?
questions.reference: Reflection tokens, which include retrieval tokens (deciding whether to retrieve) and critique tokens (judging relevance, support and usefulness).

questions.question: Does Self-RAG retrieve passages for every query?
questions.reference: No. It retrieves adaptively, on demand, only when the model decides that retrieval is needed.

questions.question: What three paradigms of RAG does the survey describe?
questions.reference: Naive RAG, Advanced RAG and Modular RAG.

questions.question: Which automated evaluation tools or frameworks for RAG does the survey mention?
questions.reference: Automated tools such as RAGAS, ARES and TruLens.
